summary: Telfair County tower beside US 441/SR 31; a 2007 archaeology report planned a road realignment around it and calls it National Register eligible.

events.note: Phase I archaeological survey for a road realignment that arcs around the tower during the US 441/SR 31 widening
Called National Register eligible in the 2007 report; eligibility is not a listing

evidence.supports: survey conducted by PBS&J for the realignment project
evidence.quote: An intensive Phase I archaeological assessment was conducted by PBS&J of the proposed Telfair Tower Realignment Project.

evidence.supports: road splits off US 441/SR 31 around the tower
evidence.quote: splits off from US 441/SR 31 to the east, around the Telfair County Lookout/Fire Tower
gently arcing to avoid the fire tower on the east side

evidence.supports: aim is to limit harm from widening US 441/SR 31; tower called National Register eligible
evidence.quote: The purpose of the proposed road realignment is to minimize impacts to the National Register eligible Telfair County Lookout/Fire Tower due to the widening of US 441/SR 31.

evidence.supports: elevation 270 ft (82 m), county Telfair, two reference numbers

sources.title: Phase I, US 441/SR 31 Firetower Realignment, Telfair County, Georgia

notes_for_editor: Only two sources. The 2007 UGA report (Keel, report 4219) is the only source describing the tower; it says National Register eligible, not listed. No build date, builder, staffing, fires, or present condition found. Status left as the record's unknown. The brief's registers (BLL US 64705, GFC US 531) come from the tnlandforms codes 'BLL-64705 gfc-531'; what BLL and GFC refer to is not stated in the sources. Not on the NHLR Georgia list (29 entries) or the FFLOS Georgia list (2 sites). The Wikipedia NRHP list for Telfair County mentions no lookout; the eligibility claim should be checked on NPGallery. A Flickr photo of the tower (2019) was seen only in search results; the page returned 404, so it is not used.
